items.q: PED = -0.6. Price decreases by 3%. What happens?
opts: Quantity demanded will rise and total sales revenue will fall
Quantity demanded will rise and total sales revenue will rise
Quantity demanded will fall and total sales revenue will fall
Quantity demanded will fall and total sales revenue will rise
items.why: Quantity rises (negative PED = inverse relationship). But revenue falls because demand is inelastic (magnitude 0.6 < 1). The quantity rise (1.8%) is smaller than the price fall (3%), so revenue drops. Inelastic demand + price decrease = revenue falls. Not enough extra volume to compensate for lower price.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Investment data for 4 projects. Which has the BEST payback?
opts: Project A (cost 12, returns 12+10+0)
Project B (cost 15, returns 10+12+15)
Project C (cost 16, returns 18+0+0)
Project D (cost 20, returns 19+15+4)
items.why: Project C: costs £16m, receives £18m in Year 1. Payback = 16/18 of a year = approximately 10.7 months. This is the fastest payback. A: pays back during year 1. B: payback in Year 2 (10+5 of 12). D: payback in Year 2 (19+1 of 15). C recovers its entire investment within Year 1. The others all take more than a year.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: According to Herzberg's 'two factor theory', which is a MOTIVATOR?
opts: Better working conditions
Greater promotion prospects
Higher basic pay
More job security
items.why: Greater promotion prospects = motivator (achievement, advancement). Working conditions (A), pay (C), and job security (D) are all hygiene factors. Promotion = motivator (intrinsic, about growth). Conditions, pay, security = hygiene (extrinsic, about environment).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Prestige Pens Ltd is a luxury fountain pen manufacturer. Its board sets a marketing objective to 'increase market share from 4% to 7% within two years'. Which of the following best explains why this objective is likely to support strategic decision-making?
opts: It identifies the target customer segment the firm should focus on, allowing the marketing team to tailor its messaging and channel selection accordingly.
It provides a measurable outcome against which marketing plans can be evaluated.
It guarantees that the firm's promotional spending will be cost-effective by linking expenditure directly to revenue targets.
It ensures the firm will achieve a higher profit margin on each unit sold by repositioning the brand at a premium price point.
items.why: A quantified, time-bound target allows managers to judge whether strategies are working and adjust accordingly. Market share growth says nothing directly about which segment to target (A) or margins (D), and setting an objective does not guarantee cost-effectiveness of spending (C).
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following best explains why a manufacturer might choose to source raw materials from a supplier located closer to its factory, even if that supplier charges a higher price?
opts: Local suppliers are required by domestic trading standards legislation to meet stricter quality control regulations than overseas alternatives, reducing the risk of faulty inputs.
Shorter supply chains reduce lead times and lower the risk of disruption, which can outweigh higher input costs.
Domestic suppliers are legally required to offer more favourable credit and payment terms, improving the manufacturer's cash flow position.
Proximity to the factory means the supplier will automatically hold more buffer stock on the manufacturer's behalf, eliminating the need for on-site storage.
items.why: A shorter supply chain reduces transport time, lowers lead times, and makes the chain more resilient to disruption (e.g. port delays, exchange rate movements). The cost premium may be justified by these operational benefits. The other options make claims that are either legally incorrect or assume automatic advantages not linked to proximity.
items.label: New question

items.q: Assuming no other changes, capacity utilisation is likely to be:
opts: Decreased by dynamic pricing and decreased by penetration pricing
Decreased by dynamic pricing and increased by penetration pricing
Increased by dynamic pricing and decreased by penetration pricing
Increased by dynamic pricing and increased by penetration pricing
items.why: Both increase utilisation. Dynamic pricing fills spare capacity during quiet times (lower off-peak prices). Penetration pricing generates high volume through low prices. Both drive higher output. Dynamic pricing fills spare capacity. Penetration pricing generates high volume.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: If Activity A is delayed by 3 days, the duration of the critical path will:
opts: Not change
Increase by 1 day
Increase by 2 days
Increase by 3 days
items.why: If Activity A is on the critical path and has no float, any delay directly extends the project by the same amount. A 3-day delay = 3-day increase in the critical path duration. Critical path activities have zero float. Any delay to a critical activity extends the whole project by the full delay amount.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Capacity utilisation is likely to be:
opts: Decreased by dynamic pricing and decreased by penetration pricing
Decreased by dynamic pricing and increased by penetration pricing
Increased by dynamic pricing and decreased by penetration pricing
Increased by dynamic pricing and increased by penetration pricing
items.why: Both increase capacity utilisation. Dynamic pricing fills off-peak capacity. Penetration pricing generates high volume. Both strategies increase sales volume = higher utilisation.

items.q: The directors of a public limited company may change it to a private limited company to:
opts: access more funds from the stock exchange.
gain limited liability.
increase the number of potential shareholders.
reduce the level of legal regulations required.
items.why: Going from PLC to Ltd reduces legal regulations. PLCs face stricter disclosure requirements, must publish accounts publicly, and comply with stock exchange listing rules. Going private removes these burdens. Option A is the opposite - going private means losing access to the stock exchange. Option B is wrong because both PLCs and Ltds already have limited liability.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: An inferior good is a product of poor quality that no rational consumer would choose to buy.

Statement 2: During a recession, demand for inferior goods typically rises as consumers' real incomes fall.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: in economics, 'inferior' refers to the relationship between income and demand (negative YED), not to quality. Many people willingly buy inferior goods. Statement 2 is true: because inferior goods have negative YED, a fall in income during a recession leads to an increase in quantity demanded as consumers substitute away from more expensive alternatives.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Primary research always produces more reliable data than secondary research because it is collected first-hand.

Statement 2: Secondary research is typically faster and less expensive to obtain than primary research.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: primary research can suffer from poorly designed questions, small samples or interviewer bias, making it less reliable than high-quality published secondary data. Statement 2 is true: secondary data (e.g. government statistics, trade reports) already exists and costs little or nothing to access, saving time and money.
items.label: New question

items.q: Luna Cosmetics creates a short, humorous video featuring a popular beauty influencer using their new lip gloss. The video is shared over two million times on social media within a week, without any additional advertising spend. Which term best describes this promotional outcome?
opts: Above-the-line promotion
Direct marketing
Viral marketing
Public relations
items.why: Viral marketing occurs when promotional content is shared rapidly and extensively by consumers themselves, creating large reach at little or no additional cost to the business. Above-the-line promotion uses paid mass-media channels; direct marketing targets individuals directly (e.g. email); public relations manages media coverage and reputation rather than consumer-to-consumer sharing.
items.label: New question

items.q: Vantage Holidays offers budget package tours. As average household incomes rise by 8%, demand for Vantage's tours falls by 4%. What does this indicate?
opts: Vantage's holidays are a normal good with a positive income elasticity of demand.
Vantage's holidays are an inferior good with a negative income elasticity of demand.
Vantage's holidays are a luxury good with an income elasticity of demand greater than 1.
Vantage's holidays have zero income elasticity of demand because the change in demand is less than the change in income.
items.why: YED = % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in income = −4% ÷ 8% = −0.5. A negative YED means demand falls as income rises, which is the definition of an inferior good. Budget products that consumers switch away from as they become wealthier are classic examples.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: A strong positive correlation between two variables proves that one causes the other.

Statement 2: Extrapolation becomes less reliable the further the forecast is made beyond the range of existing data.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: correlation shows association, not causation — a third variable may explain both. Statement 2 is true: extrapolation extends a trend line beyond observed data, and the further it extends, the more likely the underlying trend has changed, making predictions increasingly unreliable.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: In stratified sampling, the population is divided into groups and respondents are selected randomly from each group in proportion to that group's share of the population.

Statement 2: Quota sampling also divides the population into groups, but respondents within each group are selected by the interviewer rather than randomly.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are correct. The key distinction between stratified and quota sampling is the selection mechanism within each stratum: stratified uses random selection (making it probability-based), while quota sampling relies on the interviewer choosing respondents until a quota is filled, introducing potential bias.
items.label: New question

items.q: Starbucks opens 300 tea shops in America targeting existing customers. According to Ansoff:
opts: Diversification
Market development
Market penetration
Product development
items.why: New product (tea shops instead of coffee shops) targeting existing customers (American market, existing Starbucks customers) = Product Development. Tea shops are a new product offering for Starbucks, but the market is the same (existing American customers). Not diversification because the market hasn't changed.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A committee of management AND workforce representatives discussing training and conditions is a:
opts: Board of directors
Kaizen group
Trade union
Works council
items.why: A works council is a joint body of management and employee representatives that consults on workplace issues like training, conditions, and company policy. Key distinction: works council includes both management and workers. Trade unions represent workers only.

items.q: Bluebell Brewing Co. is about to launch a new craft ale. The marketing manager wants to understand the emotions and associations consumers have with the brand name before committing to a full launch. Which research method is most appropriate?
opts: A large-scale online survey with Likert-scale ratings.
Analysis of existing sales data for similar products.
Focus groups exploring consumer perceptions and feelings.
Stratified sampling of 2 000 consumers to measure purchase intent.
items.why: Qualitative methods such as focus groups are designed to uncover feelings, motivations and associations — the 'why' behind attitudes. Large surveys (A and D) produce quantitative data about what people think but not the depth of reasoning. Sales data (B) is secondary and historical, not about perceptions of a new name.
items.label: New question

items.q: Despite a significant increase in sales revenue, a product's market share falls from 60% to 50%. This product is a:
opts: Cash cow
Dog
Problem child/question mark
Star
items.why: Star. Still has high market share (50%) and revenue grew while share fell, meaning the overall market grew even faster. High share + high growth = Star. Revenue rose but share fell = market growing faster than this product. Growing market + high share = Star.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Monarch Motors cuts the price of its saloon car by 10%. Total revenue from that model subsequently falls. Which of the following conclusions is correct?
opts: Demand for the car is price elastic, so the percentage rise in quantity demanded exceeded 10%.
Demand for the car is price inelastic, so the percentage rise in quantity demanded was less than 10%.
Demand for the car is price elastic, so the percentage rise in quantity demanded was less than 10%, meaning revenue fell despite the lower price.
Demand for the car is price inelastic, so the percentage rise in quantity demanded exceeded 10%, generating sufficient volume to offset the price reduction.
items.why: When a price cut reduces total revenue, the proportional increase in quantity demanded was smaller than the proportional price cut — meaning demand is price inelastic (PED between 0 and -1). Option A would describe a revenue increase for an elastic good following a price cut.
items.label: New question
